_README: NovaFlow / Brand Guardian - least-privilege IAM policy TEMPLATE.
Phase 3.5, updated in Phase 4.1.
THIS IS A TEMPLATE, NOT A DEPLOYABLE POLICY. Every ${PLACEHOLDER} below must
be replaced with a real value before use. No account id, bucket name, or
table name has been invented here.
The bucket-naming conflict this file previously had to flag is resolved:
backend/aws_resources.py is now the single place every bucket, table, and
object prefix is defined, and infra/cloudformation/storage.yaml provisions
exactly those. infra/init_s3.py remains an unused legacy bootstrap script
that creates differently-named buckets; do not run it.
Placeholders:
${AWS_REGION}              e.g. the region in AWS_REGION
${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}          your 12-digit account id
${S3_BUCKET_NAME}          value of the S3_BUCKET_NAME env var
${DYNAMODB_FRAMES_TABLE}   value of DYNAMODB_TABLE_NAME (default NovaFlowFrames)
${DYNAMODB_PROJECTS_TABLE} value of DYNAMODB_PROJECTS_TABLE (default NovaFlowProjects)
Actions were derived from the boto3 calls the code actually makes, not from
the previous policy. Differences from infra/iam_policy.yaml:
* bedrock:InvokeModel was scoped from Resource '*' to specific models.
* DynamoDB permissions were MISSING entirely; the app could not run.
* Bucket ARNs now come from a placeholder rather than a hardcoded name.
* s3:ListBucket is constrained to the prefixes the app actually lists.
* aws:SecureTransport is required, so plaintext calls are denied.
Phase 4.1 additions, each tied to a specific new call:
* sources/* added to GetObject/PutObject - uploads are now stored in S3
instead of on the application host local disk.
* s3:DeleteObject granted for sources/* ONLY - the upload route deletes a
just-written object when the ownership write fails, so an unreachable
orphan is not left behind. Not granted for frames/ or raw/.
* dynamodb:DeleteItem granted on the frames table - a re-run prunes frame
rows left by a longer previous attempt, which would otherwise be
returned as part of the current result.
Remove this _README key before applying; it is documentation, not policy.

_comment: backend/analyzer.py and backend/audit_manager.py call invoke_model with
modelId 'amazon.nova-pro-v1:0'. The streaming variant is NOT used by any
code path; add bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream only if that
changes. The Nova Canvas entry is commented out below because the only
call site (audit_manager.remediate_frame) is disabled - grant it when
remediation is actually implemented.
put_object  - extractor.py writes frames/{video_id}/frame_NNNN.jpg
get_object  - analyzer.py reads those frames back
download_file - video_stitcher.py (GetObject under the hood)
generate_presigned_url for put_object - projects.py raw/ uploads
put_object/get_object on sources/ - source_store.py (Phase 4.1)
Scoped to the three prefixes in use so the role cannot touch anything
else in the bucket. The prefixes are defined in
backend/aws_resources.py MANAGED_PREFIXES; adding one there means
adding it here too.
delete_object - source_store.delete_source, called only when the
ownership write fails after the upload succeeded. Without it that
object would be an orphan no route can reach and no user can be
billed for.
Deliberately a separate statement scoped to sources/* so the role can
never delete an extracted frame or an agent reel. Expiring those is a
bucket lifecycle rule, not an application action.
ListBucket is a bucket-level action, constrained by prefix condition so
the role cannot enumerate the whole bucket.
put_item/update_item - extractor.py and analyzer.py
query               - app.py /violations and video_stitcher.py
scan                - analyzer.check_pending_frames (acknowledged as a
POC shortcut; remove this action once a GSI on
status replaces the scan).
delete_item         - analyzer.delete_frames_from (Phase 4.1), which
removes frame rows left by a longer previous
attempt so they are not reported as part of the
current result. Scoped to this table only.
projects.py: put_item (create), get_item (read), update_item (accept,
review, upload-init), scan (marketplace listing - also a POC shortcut).
No DeleteItem: no code path deletes a project.

Statement._comment: Scoped to this application's log group rather than logs:*:*:*.

_comment: Deliberately withheld. Add only when the corresponding feature is
actually implemented, and never to make a failing call succeed.
_NOT_GRANTED.bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream: No code path streams a response.
_NOT_GRANTED.amazon.nova-canvas-v1:0: audit_manager.remediate_frame's invoke_model call is commented out; remediation is a later phase.
_NOT_GRANTED.bedrock:ApplyGuardrail: backend/safety.py is never imported by the running app. Grant with the guardrail ARN if it is wired up.
_NOT_GRANTED.states:*: backend/aws_config.py builds a Step Functions client that no code uses.
_NOT_GRANTED.s3:CreateBucket: infra/init_s3.py is an operator bootstrap script and should run under separate administrative credentials, not the application role.
_NOT_GRANTED.s3:DeleteObject on frames/* and raw/*: Granted for sources/* only, for orphan cleanup. No code path deletes a frame or a reel; expiring those is a bucket lifecycle rule.
_NOT_GRANTED.dynamodb:DeleteItem on the projects tabl: No code path deletes a project. Granted on the frames table only, for stale-frame pruning.
_NOT_GRANTED.dynamodb:CreateTable: Table provisioning is an operator action; see docs/SECURITY_OPERATIONS.md.
_NOT_GRANTED.logs:CreateLogGroup: Create the log group once, out of band, so the running role cannot create arbitrary groups.

_comment: These are bucket and account settings, not identity-policy statements.
They are listed so they are not forgotten; apply them to the bucket
itself. As of Phase 4.1, infra/cloudformation/storage.yaml applies all
of them, so provisioning through that template satisfies this list.
infra/init_s3.py, the legacy script, applies none of them.
_BUCKET_HARDENING_NOT_EXPRESSIBLE_HERE.PublicAccessBlockConfiguration: BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, RestrictPublicBuckets - all true.
_BUCKET_HARDENING_NOT_EXPRESSIBLE_HERE.BucketEncryption: SSE-S3 (AES256) at minimum, or SSE-KMS with a CMK.
_BUCKET_HARDENING_NOT_EXPRESSIBLE_HERE.Versioning: Enabled, so an overwritten frame or reel is recoverable.
_BUCKET_HARDENING_NOT_EXPRESSIBLE_HERE.BucketPolicy: Add an explicit Deny for aws:SecureTransport=false at the bucket level too, so the constraint does not depend on the caller's identity policy.
_BUCKET_HARDENING_NOT_EXPRESSIBLE_HERE.LifecycleConfiguration: Expire or transition sources/, frames/ and raw/ objects per the retention decision in docs/SECURITY_OPERATIONS.md. infra/cloudformation/storage.yaml expresses these as parameters.
_BUCKET_HARDENING_NOT_EXPRESSIBLE_HERE.ServerAccessLogging_or_CloudTrailDataEve: Needed to audit who read a reel; neither is configured today.
